host_scope: one disposable GitHub-hosted Ubuntu24.04 x86_64 VM; requires two distinct physical CPU cores; two isolated local network namespaces per case; no WAN generalization

behavior.positive_gates: real tun/ovpn path and source-route; exact payload+echo before/after rekey/reconnect; no old duplicate/corrupt deliveries; actual TLS/key events and HIA entry trace when used
behavior.continuity_loss_policy: retain every missing sequence and error through forced reconnect; phase-specific fresh probes require full delivery; continuity flow alone never establishes success

udp_acceptance.interpretation: both send directions must offer at least 95% of the declared rate; both local receivers must deliver at least 95% with at most 1% packet loss; every under-offer or degraded receipt remains a failure

performance.cpu_affinity: server and client: one allowed logical CPU from each of two distinct physical cores; OpenVPN and local iperf endpoint share that role CPU; identical mapping for every arm; exact package/core topology recorded
performance.outlier_policy: retain all trials, startup, losses, resets, failures and raw iperf fields; no selection or confidence inflation
performance.claim_limit: finite paired virtual-network observations on one shared hosted VM; not production, WAN, hardware-NIC or cross-host performance qualification

profile.fallback: record failure; do not relabel gprof as complete process/kernel profile

cleanup: only recorded case PIDs/groups and recorded namespace name+inode; remove private-work PKI; preserve public raw failures

p2p_dispatch.policy: When SOCKET_READ and TUN_READ are both ready, alternate the next read by context-local last-read state. Pending SOCKET_WRITE/TUN_WRITE retain priority. DCO_READ is unchanged.
p2p_dispatch.claim_limit: A controlled poll-readiness counterexample motivates this patch; only a full target run can establish its effect on real tunnel performance.
